title: Rational ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison for a finite-projective summand
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $t\in A$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative $A$-algebras. Write $D(R)$ for the derived category of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with the $A$-linear structure induced by $A\to R$ [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], and $Q_t:D(R)\to D(R)[1/t]$ for its scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Fix a K-injective resolution $j:R[0]\to I$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For an $R$-module sheaf $F$ put $B(F)=\mathcal Hom_R(F,R)[0]$ and $T(F)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(F[0],I)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]; postcomposition with $j$ gives the chain map $c_F:B(F)\to T(F)$. Suppose that for some integer $m\geq0$ there are morphisms $i:Q_t(F[0])\to Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])$ and $p:Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])\to Q_t(F[0])$ with $pi=1$. Then $Q_t(c_F)$ is an isomorphism. Moreover $Q_t(B(F))$ is a direct summand of $Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])$ in the same sense as in the hypothesis: there are morphisms $i':Q_t(B(F))\to Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])$ and $p':Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])\to Q_t(B(F))$ of $D(R)[1/t]$ with $p'i'=1$. The comparison $c_F$ is natural under module maps, and this naturality extends $A[1/t]$-linearly to maps in the scalar localization of the degree-zero module subcategory.

The rational extension is agent-written, not asserted verbatim by the Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Put $E=R^{\oplus m}$. Apply the bounded-above finite-projective sheaf Hom model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] to $E[0]$ and $R[0]$; with both bounds equal to $0$, it identifies the derived internal Hom from $E[0]$ to $R[0]$ with $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E[0],R[0])$. By the definition of derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the same object is represented by $T(E)=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E[0],I)$, and the comparison between these representatives is postcomposition with the resolution map $j$, namely $c_E$. Evaluation on the standard basis identifies $c_E$ with the direct sum of $m$ copies of $j$; since $j:R[0]\to I$ is a K-injective resolution, this is an isomorphism in $D(R)$. Applying $Q_t$ preserves this isomorphism. The case $m=0$ is the same calculation with zero complexes.

source.place: Tag 08JI, lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free; degree-zero finite-free specialization, with the K-injective model from Section 08J7

proof.text: For a module map $u:F\to G$, both $B$ and $T$ act by precomposition, and the square expressing $c$-naturality, $c_F\circ B(u)=T(u)\circ c_G$, commutes because on a homogeneous local section $\phi$ and $x$ both routes send it to $j(\phi(u(x)))$. Thus $c$ is a natural transformation between the contravariant functors $B$ and $T$ on the degree-zero module subcategory; both functors are $A$-linear, since precomposition with $au$ is $a$ times precomposition with $u$, and $D(R)$ and $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}\to D(R)$ are $A$-linear [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. By full faithfulness of $M\mapsto M[0]$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(F[0],G[0])=\operatorname{Hom}_R(F,G)$, so every morphism $F[0]\to G[0]$ of $D(R)$ is a module map and $B$, $T$, $c$ are defined on the full subcategory of $D(R)$ of degree-zero objects. The scalar localization has Hom modules $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,L)\otimes_A A[1/t]$ and composition $(f\otimes a)\circ(g\otimes b)=(f\circ g)\otimes ab$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Extending $B$, $T$ by $u\otimes a\mapsto B(u)\otimes a$, $T(u)\otimes a$ (well defined by $A$-linearity) and $c$ by $c_F\otimes1$ makes the same naturality square commute for every localized morphism $u\otimes a$, both sides being $(c_F\circ B(u))\otimes a=(T(u)\circ c_G)\otimes a$; the identity and composition laws follow from the displayed localization formulas.

source.place: Sections 08J7 and 0A8X, functoriality of internal Hom and Hom-complex; scalar-localized extension is written out from the definition

proof.text: Work now in the localized category and abbreviate the images of $c_E$ and of all maps by the same letters. Applying the contravariant functors $B$ and $T$ to the given $i:F[0]\to E[0]$ and $p:E[0]\to F[0]$ gives maps $B(p):B(F)\to B(E)$, $B(i):B(E)\to B(F)$, $T(p):T(F)\to T(E)$, and $T(i):T(E)\to T(F)$, with $B(i)B(p)=1$ and $T(i)T(p)=1$. Naturality from the preceding step gives $T(p)c_F=c_EB(p)$ and $T(i)c_E=c_FB(i)$. Since $c_E$ is invertible by Step 1, define $d=B(i)\circ c_E^{-1}\circ T(p):T(F)\to B(F)$. Then $d c_F=B(i)c_E^{-1}T(p)c_F=B(i)c_E^{-1}c_EB(p)=B(i)B(p)=1$ and $c_Fd=c_FB(i)c_E^{-1}T(p)=T(i)c_Ec_E^{-1}T(p)=T(i)T(p)=1$, so $c_F=Q_t(c_F)$ is an isomorphism. The maps $i'=B(p):B(F)\to B(E)$ and $p'=B(i):B(E)\to B(F)$ satisfy $p'i'=B(i)B(p)=1$, so they exhibit $Q_t(B(F))$ as a direct summand of $Q_t(B(E))$ in the sense of the statement, and evaluation on the standard basis gives the module isomorphism $\mathcal Hom_R(R^{\oplus m},R)\cong R^{\oplus m}$, hence $B(E)\cong R^{\oplus m}[0]$; composing $i'$, $p'$ with this isomorphism and its inverse gives the required maps to and from $Q_t(R^{\oplus m}[0])$. For $m=0$ both sides are zero objects.
